newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.39 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.39 pct to new record.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's stock exchange firmed on selective buying to an all-time high close of 83,828.67 on Friday, compared to a previous record of 83,772.33 on October 23.
The IMKB-100 gained 323.30 points, or 0.39 percent from Thursday when it leapt 2.51 percent on strong selective buys. But it fell from an early high of 84,747 on profit-taking, brokers said.
Trade volume rose sharply to 21.29 trillion lira from Thursday's 17.39 trillion.
Brokers said the market managed to keep part of the early gains with the help of selective buys despite the profit-taking.
"Players switched to cheaper shares to sustain the rise. The index may pierce 85,000 resistance next week," said Erol Guney from Yurtbank.

The market index had surged 29.3 percent, breaking ten record closes from September 13 to October 23 in a medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level. But it drifted lower in range-trading after failing to pierce stiff 85,000 barrier on October 31.
Over the week, the index rose 1.5 percent after last week's 0.83 percent gain.
Brokers said the resignation of Interior Minister Mehmet Agar did not affect the market in the afternoon.

Top actives were largely state-owed petroleum refiner Tupras, up 1,500 lira at 22,750, utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 1,000 lira at 82,000, leading industrial conglomerate Koc Holding, down 1,000 lira at 19,500 and Turkish Airlines, down 500 at 23,750.
Together, the four made up 25 percent of the total volume.

Of the 226 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 115 to 68 and 43 closed stable. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.55 percent to 88,316.47 and the 15-share financial index edged 0.02 percent higher to 81,643.64.
